Introduction

The Dab Tool Set — dab tool set for handling concentrates. This record gives the full description, specification, science proof, math proof, and care routine for this supply.

History

The Signature design for the dab tool set starts where the public record leaves off, with a working supply whose parts are already known, and asks how those parts could be made as one matched set. The design keeps the job, dab tool set for handling concentrates, and re-specifies the parts: five interchangeable tools on one handle: a flat paddle, a pointed pick, a scoop, a spatula blade and a shovel, plus a glass bubble carb cap, a silicone mat and a zippered case. The design history is therefore short, because the supply itself is old and the design is new: the public versions established what works, the guides established the routine, and the Signature design reorganises those findings into a single dimension sheet, handle 100 mm long; each tool head 30 mm long; paddle 8 mm wide; pick tip 1 mm across; carb cap 25 mm across; case 170 mm by 110 mm by 30 mm. Nothing in that history involves a prototype, a test, or a sale, and the record is careful to say so. A design study has a history of decisions, not a history of products, and its decisions are recorded here so that a builder can follow them, challenge them, or replace them with better ones.

The supply in detail

In detail, the Signature design is a drawing in words: a complete specification of a product that has not been built. The design specifies five interchangeable tools on one handle: a flat paddle, a pointed pick, a scoop, a spatula blade and a shovel, plus a glass bubble carb cap, a silicone mat and a zippered case. The materials are grade 2 titanium tips, stainless steel handle, borosilicate glass carb cap, food-grade silicone mat, and the design dimensions are handle 100 mm long; each tool head 30 mm long; paddle 8 mm wide; pick tip 1 mm across; carb cap 25 mm across; case 170 mm by 110 mm by 30 mm. How the design is intended to work is this: the tool tip picks up, scoops or spreads a measured piece of concentrate and carries it to the heated banger, and the carb cap then covers the banger to restrict airflow, lower the pressure inside, and direct vapour across the hot surface. The design routine follows the same sequence as the public version, so that a user who knows the public supply can use the Signature design without learning a new method. The planned variants are the single titanium dabber; dabber and carb cap combo tool; multi-tool folding set; glass sword dabber with a titanium tip, and each is a scaling of the same drawing, not a new design. The design label is part of the detail, not an afterthought: every figure in this record is a design target, every material is a specification, and nothing here has been measured on a built unit. A reader who wants a tested product should look at the public record instead.

Spec

  • Materials: grade 2 titanium tips, stainless steel handle, borosilicate glass carb cap, food-grade silicone mat.
  • Dimensions: handle 100 mm long; each tool head 30 mm long; paddle 8 mm wide; pick tip 1 mm across; carb cap 25 mm across; case 170 mm by 110 mm by 30 mm.
  • Mechanism: the tool tip picks up, scoops or spreads a measured piece of concentrate and carries it to the heated banger, and the carb cap then covers the banger to restrict airflow, lower the pressure inside, and direct vapour across the hot surface.
  • Use: choose the tip that matches the concentrate texture, paddle for crumbly material and pick for sticky material, load the banger without touching the hot glass, cap it, and wipe the tip clean with a cotton swab while it is still warm.
  • Care: wipe tips after every session, soak metal tips in isopropyl alcohol when residue hardens, never use a steel tool on a hot quartz banger with force, since a hard scrape can chip it, and store tips in the case so the fine points do not bend.
  • Variants: single titanium dabber; dabber and carb cap combo tool; multi-tool folding set; glass sword dabber with a titanium tip.

Science proof

The Signature design uses the same science as the public version, because the physics does not change when a product is redesigned, and the design study checks that the chosen materials and dimensions respect it. The solvent chemistry is unchanged: isopropyl alcohol dissolves resin because its polar hydroxyl group and its carbon chain can both interact with the tar-like film, and coarse salt stays undissolved in alcohol, so it keeps its edges and scours. The mechanical science is also unchanged: bristles clean by friction, a mesh separates by size, a seal contains odour by compression, and a lock resists opening by counting combinations. What the design adds is a check that the numbers fit the science. The reach must exceed the airway, the aperture must sit between the particle sizes it should pass and the ones it should hold back, the water depth must cover the percolator without reaching the mouthpiece, and the heat capacity of a tool must be small enough that it does not steal the heat of the surface it touches. Where the public record reports what guides have observed, the Signature record states what the design intends, and it labels the difference plainly. The science proof therefore proves the design is consistent with known physics, not that it has been tested, and the demo computes the numbers that show that consistency.

Math proof

The Signature arithmetic is the same kind of check as the public arithmetic, applied to design targets rather than measured products. The formal equation is Q = m x c x delta_T, with m = 18 g, c = 0.523 J/g/K and delta_T = 200 K, so Q is about 1,883 J. The heat a titanium tool can absorb equals its mass times its specific heat capacity times the temperature change.. Each design number is checked against the number it must beat. A reach is checked against the airway it must follow, a volume against the bowl or chamber it must fill, an aperture against the particle sizes on either side of it, and a combination count against the number of dials on the lock. The demo performs those checks in code: it takes the design figures from the key figures list, computes the derived quantities, prints each with its name, and then repeats the whole computation with the same fixed seed and prints a SHA-256 digest of both runs. Because the seed is fixed, the two digests match, which shows the computation is reproducible. That is the whole claim of the math proof: the design is arithmetically consistent, and any reader can repeat the check. It does not show that a prototype would pass a physical test, and the record says so plainly, because a design study that pretended its arithmetic was a test would be misleading.

Use and care

Use and care, as designed: Choose the tip that matches the concentrate texture, paddle for crumbly material and pick for sticky material, load the banger without touching the hot glass, cap it, and wipe the tip clean with a cotton swab while it is still warm. Wipe tips after every session, soak metal tips in isopropyl alcohol when residue hardens, never use a steel tool on a hot quartz banger with force, since a hard scrape can chip it, and store tips in the case so the fine points do not bend. The design adds storage rules of its own: each tool returns to its shaped pocket, the case stays closed when it is not in use, and the consumable parts are replaced from the same specification, so that a replacement cleaner or screen matches the original. Because this is a design study, the care instructions are design intentions, not tested instructions, and a prototype test would be expected to correct them before the design is called a product.

Design-study label

This record is a Signature design study. It describes a Signature-made product design that has not been manufactured, tested, or sold. Its dimensions and figures are design targets, not measured results, and it is not presented as a real product or as established fact. Legal note: laws on cannabis and cannabis accessories vary by jurisdiction; check local law before buying, carrying, or using this item.

demo.code:
import hashlib, json, math, random

TOOL_MASS_G = 18
TITANIUM_CP = 0.523
DELTA_T_K = 200
PICK_TIP_MM = 1
LOAD_FORCE_N = 0.5
TOOLS_IN_SET = 5

def compute(seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    heat_j = round(TOOL_MASS_G * TITANIUM_CP * DELTA_T_K, 1)
    tip_radius_m = (PICK_TIP_MM / 2.0) / 1000.0
    tip_area_m2 = math.pi * tip_radius_m ** 2
    tip_pressure_pa = round(LOAD_FORCE_N / tip_area_m2, 1)
    load_g = round(TOOL_MASS_G * 0.02, 2)
    per_tool_j = round(heat_j / TOOLS_IN_SET, 1)
    cool_seconds = round(heat_j / 25.0, 1)
    wobble = round(rng.uniform(0.98, 1.02), 3)
    out = {
        "tool_mass_g": TOOL_MASS_G,
        "titanium_specific_heat_j_per_g_k": TITANIUM_CP,
        "temperature_change_k": DELTA_T_K,
        "heat_absorbed_j": heat_j,
        "heat_per_tool_j": per_tool_j,
        "pick_tip_pressure_pa": tip_pressure_pa,
        "typical_load_grams": load_g,
        "cooling_time_seconds": cool_seconds,
        "tools_in_set": TOOLS_IN_SET,
        "measurement_jitter": wobble,
    }
    return out

def main():
    first = compute(7)
    second = compute(7)
    for key, value in first.items():
        print(f"{key}: {value}")
    d1 = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(first, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
    d2 = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(second, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
    print(f"digest_run_1: {d1}")
    print(f"digest_run_2: {d2}")
    print("Deterministic: MATCH" if d1 == d2 else "Deterministic: MISMATCH")

main()

It starts from the dimension sheet, handle 100 mm long; each tool head 30 mm long; paddle 8 mm wide; pick tip 1 mm across; carb cap 25 mm across; case 170 mm by 110 mm by 30 mm, and checks that each tool reaches the space it must clean, that the case holds every tool in its pocket, and that the materials, grade 2 titanium tips, stainless steel handle, borosilicate glass carb cap, food-grade silicone mat, are compatible with each other and with the pipes they will touch. Next it assigns each tool one job and one job only, so that the cleaner cleans, the brush brushes, and the reamer reams, and no tool is asked to do work it is not shaped for. The routine is then written as a sequence, left to right across the case, so that a user who follows the pockets follows the method. A physical prototype would still be needed before any claim about how the design feels in the hand or how long it lasts, and this record makes no such claim.
problem: The Signature design starts from the same problem as the public record, residue that narrows airways and thickens bowl cake, but it treats the problem as a design brief rather than a maintenance chore. The brief asks for a kit in which every tool is sized to the space it works in, so that no step of the clean needs a borrowed or improvised tool. The design problem has three parts. First, reach: the longest tool must follow the full length of the airway it serves, with enough length left in the hand to control it. Second, force: the scrubbing parts must be firm enough to lift hardened residue and soft enough not to scratch glass, wood, or glaze. Third, order: the tools must be stored in the sequence they are used, so the kit teaches its own routine. As a design study, this record does not claim the design has been built or tested. It claims only that the geometry works on paper, that the materials are compatible, and that the routine is complete, and it invites a builder to test it before calling it a product.

"""The Dab Tool Set — working program.

Computes the same quantities as the record demo: the design numbers for
this supply, from the figures in the record. Standard library only, no
network. Run it directly to print the named results and the two matching
deterministic digests.
"""
import hashlib, json, math, random

TOOL_MASS_G = 18
TITANIUM_CP = 0.523
DELTA_T_K = 200
PICK_TIP_MM = 1
LOAD_FORCE_N = 0.5
TOOLS_IN_SET = 5

def compute(seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    heat_j = round(TOOL_MASS_G * TITANIUM_CP * DELTA_T_K, 1)
    tip_radius_m = (PICK_TIP_MM / 2.0) / 1000.0
    tip_area_m2 = math.pi * tip_radius_m ** 2
    tip_pressure_pa = round(LOAD_FORCE_N / tip_area_m2, 1)
    load_g = round(TOOL_MASS_G * 0.02, 2)
    per_tool_j = round(heat_j / TOOLS_IN_SET, 1)
    cool_seconds = round(heat_j / 25.0, 1)
    wobble = round(rng.uniform(0.98, 1.02), 3)
    out = {
        "tool_mass_g": TOOL_MASS_G,
        "titanium_specific_heat_j_per_g_k": TITANIUM_CP,
        "temperature_change_k": DELTA_T_K,
        "heat_absorbed_j": heat_j,
        "heat_per_tool_j": per_tool_j,
        "pick_tip_pressure_pa": tip_pressure_pa,
        "typical_load_grams": load_g,
        "cooling_time_seconds": cool_seconds,
        "tools_in_set": TOOLS_IN_SET,
        "measurement_jitter": wobble,
    }
    return out


class DabToolSet:
    """Model of the dab tool set."""

    def __init__(self, seed=7):
        self.seed = seed

    def run(self):
        """Run the computation twice and print the named results."""
        first = compute(self.seed)
        second = compute(self.seed)
        for key, value in first.items():
            print(f"{key}: {value}")
        d1 = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(first, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
        d2 = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(second, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
        print(f"digest_run_1: {d1}")
        print(f"digest_run_2: {d2}")
        print("Deterministic: MATCH" if d1 == d2 else "Deterministic: MISMATCH")
        return first


if __name__ == "__main__":
    DabToolSet().run()
proof_sketch: The dimensions are checked by direct comparison: the reaching tool against the space it must reach, the solvent or water volume against the container it must fill, and the mesh or bore size against the particles or airflow it must pass. Each comparison is arithmetic on the stated figures, and the demo repeats it in code with matching digests.
results_reported: As a design study, this record reports design results, not test results: the geometry checks out, the materials are compatible, and the routine is complete on paper. The demo attached to this record computes the design numbers, reach, volume, aperture, or combinations, from the dimension sheet, and prints them so that any reader can repeat the arithmetic. The expected result of that computation is shown as the expected output, and the demo runs the computation twice with a fixed seed and prints matching digests, so that the arithmetic is reproducible. What the design does not report is any physical test: no prototype was built, no cleaning trial was run, and no wear test was done. Any claim that the design cleans better, lasts longer, or feels better than an existing kit would be untested, and this record does not make it. The honest result of a design study is a complete, checkable drawing in words and numbers, ready for a builder to prototype, and that is what this record delivers.

skeptical_analysis: A design study deserves the same scepticism as a product claim, and more, because nothing has been built yet. First, paper geometry is not proof of comfort: a handle that measures well can still feel wrong, and a case that packs neatly on a drawing can be awkward to open with one hand. Second, material compatibility on paper is not durability in use, and a mesh that is rated for a given aperture can still stretch, a seal can still take a set, and a lock can still jam. Third, the arithmetic in this record checks dimensions and counts, not performance: it shows that a cleaner reaches, that a screen passes a particle, or that a lock has a thousand combinations, and it does not show that the clean is faster or the sift is purer. Fourth, the design inherits the limits of the public version it is based on, including the material warnings, and it adds a new one, which is that an unbuilt design has no failure history to learn from. The honest use of this record is as a starting drawing for a prototype, to be tested, corrected, and only then called a product.
